question: FDI in Multi Brand Retail Trade is permitted up to what limit? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (24/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: 49%
51%
100%
74%
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 51%

Explanation:
In India, FDI (Foreign Direct Investment) in Multi Brand Retail Trade is permitted up to 51%. This limit was set by the government and notified in the year 2012. Several conditions apply to FDI in this sector, such as a minimum investment of $100 million, at least 50% of the investment to be in cold storage or back-end infrastructure, and at least 30% of products to be sourced from small industries. This policy was designed to boost foreign investment in the retail sector and improve the supply chain.

☛ FDI limit in Single Brand Retail Trade → 100%
☛ Year when FDI in Multi Brand Retail was allowed up to 51% → 2012
☛ Minimum investment required for Multi Brand Retail FDI → $100 million
☛ Mandatory sourcing percentage from small industries in Multi Brand Retail FDI → 30%

question: Which of the following is NOT correct about the scheme of Jan Shikshan Sansthan of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE)? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (19/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: It focuses on identifying and promoting traditional skills in the districts through skilling/upskilling
It focuses on creation of a pool of master trainers
It is implemented through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs)
It focuses to improve the occupational skills and technical knowledge of the non/neo literates and persons having rudimentary level of education
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It is implemented through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs)

Explanation:
The Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) scheme under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) aims to provide vocational skills to non-literates, neo-literates, and persons with rudimentary education. It also focuses on identifying and promoting traditional skills in districts. The scheme is implemented through Jan Shikshan Sansthans, not through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs). ITIs are separate institutions for industrial training. Hence, this statement is incorrect. While the scheme also aims to create a pool of master trainers, its implementation is not via ITIs.

question_hi: कौशल विकास एवं उद्यमिता मंत्रालय (MSDE) की जन शिक्षण संस्थान योजना के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही नहीं है? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (19/03/2026) Shift 2)
options_hi: इसका उद्देश्य कौशल विकास/कौशल उन्नयन के माध्यम से जिलों में पारंपरिक कौशलों की पहचान करना और उन्हें बढ़ावा देना है।
इसका मुख्य उद्देश्य कुशल प्रशिक्षकों का एक समूह तैयार करना है।

solution_hi:

Explanation:
जन शिक्षण संस्थान (JSS) योजना कौशल विकास एवं उद्यमिता मंत्रालय (MSDE) के अंतर्गत आती है। इसका उद्देश्य निरक्षरों, नव-साक्षरों और प्राथमिक शिक्षा वाले व्यक्तियों को व्यावसायिक कौशल प्रदान करना है, साथ ही पारंपरिक कौशलों की पहचान एवं संवर्धन करना है। यह योजना ITIs के माध्यम से नहीं, बल्कि जन शिक्षण संस्थानों के माध्यम से कार्यान्वित की जाती है। ITIs अलग संस्थान हैं जो औद्योगिक प्रशिक्षण देते हैं। अतः यह कथन गलत है। JSS का ध्यान कुशल प्रशिक्षकों का समूह तैयार करने पर भी है, लेकिन इसका कार्यान्वयन ITIs से नहीं होता।

question: The 'Middle-Income Trap' refers to ____________. (RRB JE (19/02/2026) Shift 3)
options: Struggle to attain high income status
Over-reliance on foreign aid
Exclusive focus on agriculture
Rapid transition to high-income status
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Struggle to attain high income status

Explanation:
The Middle-Income Trap refers to a situation where a country, after reaching middle-income levels, struggles to transition to high-income status. This occurs when the country's competitiveness declines, innovation and productivity stagnate, and structural transformation halts. The economy fails to shift from low-cost labor and resource-based growth to value-added production. The concept was popularized by the World Bank and observed in countries like Malaysia and Brazil. To escape this trap, focus on education, R&D, infrastructure, and institutional reforms is crucial.

☛ Is India in a Middle-Income Trap? → Not yet, but risk exists
☛ Which indicator is linked to Middle-Income Trap? → Per capita income

question: The Taj Mahal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in which Indian State/UT? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (22/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Uttar Pradesh
Madhya Pradesh
Delhi
Rajasthan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Uttar Pradesh

Explanation:
The Taj Mahal is located in the city of Agra, Uttar Pradesh, on the banks of the Yamuna River. It was built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan between 1632 and 1653 in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. The structure is made of white marble and its architecture is a blend of Persian, Islamic, and Indian styles. The Taj Mahal was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983. It is one of India's most famous monuments and attracts millions of tourists every year. It is also listed among the Seven Wonders of the World.

question: Ustad Ahmad Lahori is renowned as the chief architect of which UNESCO World Heritage Site? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Humayun's Tomb, Delhi
Fatehpur Sikri, Agra
Taj Mahal, Agra
Jaisalmer Fort, Rajasthan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Taj Mahal, Agra

Explanation:
Ustad Ahmad Lahori was a renowned Mughal architect, known as the chief architect of the Taj Mahal. The Taj Mahal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in Agra, India. It was commissioned by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. Built from white marble, its construction began in 1632 CE and was completed in 1653 CE. It is considered one of the Seven Wonders of the World. Besides Lahori, Persian architect Ustad Isa is also credited with contributing to its design. The Taj Mahal is famous for its symmetrical architecture and beauty, attracting millions of visitors annually. It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

question: Amir Khusrau, the famous historian, said about a particular language that 'common people do not know it, only the Brahmanas do'. Which of the following languages did the historian talk about? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (18/03/2026) Shift 1)

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sanskrit

Explanation:

question: Consider a hypothetical population of rabbits experiencing logistic growth. If the carrying capacity of their environment is 1000 individuals and the current population is 500, what would you expect to happen to the population? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (16/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: The population will decline rapidly due to resource depletion.
The population will continue to grow exponentially without any constraints.
The population will experience a sudden crash followed by a rapid rebound.
The population growth will slow down and eventually stabilize near the carrying capacity.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The population growth will slow down and eventually stabilize near the carrying capacity.

Explanation:
This question is based on the logistic growth model. When the population is at half the carrying capacity (500/1000), the growth rate is at its maximum. However, as the population approaches the carrying capacity, the growth rate slows down due to limited resources. Eventually, the population stabilizes around the carrying capacity, where birth and death rates balance. Exponential growth only occurs when resources are unlimited. Therefore, the population will slow and stabilize.

☛ What is carrying capacity (K)? → The maximum population size that the environment can sustain indefinitely

☛ Exponential vs Logistic growth → Exponential: unlimited resources; Logistic: limited resources
☛ Reason for population stabilization → Resource limitation and competition

☛ वहन क्षमता (K) क्या है? → वह अधिकतम जनसंख्या आकार जो पर्यावरण स्थायी रूप से सहन कर सकता है
☛ वृद्धिघाती वृद्धि में अधिकतम वृद्धि दर कब होती है? → जब N = K/2
☛ चरघाती वृद्धि बनाम वृद्धिघाती वृद्धि → चरघाती में संसाधन असीमित, वृद्धिघाती में सीमित
☛ जनसंख्या स्थिरीकरण का कारण → संसाधनों की सीमा और प्रतिस्पर्धा
